name: Saimaluu-Tash
near: Kazarman — the centre of Toguz-Toro District and the start of all routes: ~38 km by dirt road to the foot of the mountain (Nomad's Land), then a climb on foot or horseback. To Kazarman: 157 km from Jalal-Abad, 220 km from Naryn (CBT Kazarman).
elev: About 3000–3200 m: a plateau “above 3000 m” (too.kg, CBT Kyrgyzstan); travellers in 2025 — about 3100 m with the trail starting at ~2000 m (takali.org). The climb from Kazarman is about 1970 m (Nomad's Land).
short: One of the largest “galleries” of rock art in Central Asia — more than 90,000 images from the Bronze and early Iron Ages on basalt boulders in a high-mountain tract of the Fergana Range; accessible only in summer.
desc: Saimaluu-Tash (“patterned stones”) is a high-mountain tract on the eastern slope of the Fergana Range, where more than 90,000 petroglyphs have been carved into black basalt boulders (too.kg, CBT Kyrgyzstan). The drawings are dated from the 3rd–1st millennia BC to the 1st–8th centuries AD: animals, hunting scenes, people, solar signs and “sun-headed” deities, geometric symbols. Since 2001 the territory has been a state nature park (decree no. 249 of 25.05.2001; boundaries clarified in 2018, 24.kg). There are proposals to digitize the site and nominate it for the UNESCO World Heritage List (Kaktus) — it is not on the list yet, despite CBT's wording. Because of snow, the tract is accessible only from about mid-July to mid-August (CBT Kazarman); modern vandalism is visible on the stones (takali.org, 2025).
guide: Saimaluu-Tash is an expedition, not an excursion: after 38 km of dirt road from Kazarman you face 5 hours in the saddle or a steep 4–6 hour climb on foot, and on the plateau a night in a tent at 3000+ m. But you will find yourself among tens of thousands of drawings up to 4–5 thousand years old: look for bulls with huge horns, ploughing scenes and “sun-headed” people. Plan the trip for the second half of July — early August: in 2023 and 2024 snow lay longer than usual. Take a guide from Kazarman — the trail and the river ford have to be found anew in different years. Don't touch or trace the drawings — they are already being spoiled by modern inscriptions.
see: Fields of basalt boulders with petroglyphs (more than 90,000 images): ibexes, bulls, horses, hunting and ploughing scenes, chariots, solar signs and anthropomorphic “sun-headed” figures; alpine meadows and views of the Fergana Range; the night sky from the plateau (too.kg; CBT Kyrgyzstan).
skip: You don't have 2–3 days and the physical fitness for a climb to 3000+ m with a night in a tent. You aren't travelling in July — August: the rest of the time the petroglyphs are under snow. Simpler petroglyphs will do for you — for example the open-air museum in Cholpon-Ata.
diff: Hard: 7.5 km one way with a gain of ~1100 m (from ~2000 to ~3100 m), 4–6 h up and ~2 h down, steep slippery sections, fords, and at the start of the season thickets of thistles and nettles (takali.org, 07.2025). The horse option is 2 × 2.5 h in the saddle via Besh-Beren (Nomad's Land). A night at altitude is required.
when: The window is roughly mid-July to mid-August (CBT Kazarman); too.kg and CBT Kyrgyzstan say July — August; Nomad's Land offers a tour from 15 June to 30 September. In 2023 and 2024 the snow melted late — travellers advise going from mid-July (takali.org, 2025).
hours: No schedule: a nature park, round-the-clock access in season. A park ranger collects a fee at the fenced parking lot at the start of the trail (takali.org, 2025). Out of season (September — June) the approach is effectively closed by snow.
daytime: Leave Kazarman early in the morning (Nomad's Land) to reach the petroglyphs by noon. The drawings read better in the slanting light of morning and evening; in the evening there can be a strong wind on the plateau (takali.org).
how: 1) To Kazarman: from Jalal-Abad — 157 km; since 01.06.2026 the alternative North — South road Balykchy — Jalal-Abad (433 km) with the Kok-Art tunnel (~3.9 km) has been temporarily open, traffic 06:00–20:00, a toll of 100–5000 som depending on the vehicle, in operation until November 2026 (Kaktus, lada.kz 01.06.2026). From Naryn — 220 km (CBT Kazarman). 2) Kazarman — the foot of the mountain: ~38 km on a gravel road (Nomad's Land; too.kg — first ~10 km west). 3) The climb: on foot 7.5 km / 4–6 h or on horseback ~5 h via Besh-Beren.
needcar: Yes: to Kazarman — marshrutka (minibus)/taxi, from Kazarman to the start of the trail — an SUV or an arrangement with a local driver (travellers in 2025 hitchhiked). Then on foot or by horse.
self: Technically yes (travellers did it on their own in 2025, hitchhiking to the trail), but the trail is poorly marked and the fords and snow bridges change from year to year — a CBT Kazarman guide is recommended. No border permit is required (outside the border zone). The park fee is collected at the parking lot.
roadtype: To Kazarman — the paved new alternative North — South road (some sections are still under construction, 2026 restrictions); Kazarman — foot of the mountain — ~38 km of gravel/dirt road (Nomad's Land); then a mountain trail with steep slippery sections and fords.
traveltime: Jalal-Abad — Kazarman: 157 km, roughly 3–4 h (estimate); Balykchy — Jalal-Abad on the new road ~6 h (lada.kz, 2026). Kazarman — foot of the mountain: ~1–1.5 h on dirt road (estimate). The climb: 4–6 h on foot / ~5 h on horseback; the descent ~2 h (takali.org 2025; Nomad's Land). Plan at least 2 days with a night out.
stay: At the petroglyphs — tents only (camping 300 som, takali.org 2025); boil water from streams and springs (too.kg). In Kazarman — guesthouses at $15–45/night depending on the season and meals (visitkyrgyzstan.org); Guesthouse Islam (in the Nomad's Land catalogue); book via CBT Kazarman. In July — August cycling groups take up the rooms — book in advance.
net: There is no mobile signal at the petroglyphs (too.kg). Kazarman has coverage (operator not confirmed).
entry: 300–400 som for entry and 300 som for camping — collected by the nature park ranger at the parking lot at the start of the trail (takali.org, 07.2025). The park's official price list was not found.
transfer: A guide with a day trip — 4000–9000 som (2025 quotes, takali.org); the Kok-Art tunnel — from 100 som for cars (2026). Prices of marshrutkas (minibuses) to Kazarman and of a jeep Kazarman — foot of the mountain are not published.
bring: A tent, a warm sleeping bag and a down jacket (nights are cold at 3100 m), long trousers and sleeves (thistles, nettles), trekking poles, shoes for fords, a stove and a water filter/tablets, cash (300–700 som for park fees), sun protection. Food for all days — there is nothing on the plateau.
warn: The access window is about a month (mid-July — mid-August); outside it there is snow. Altitude 3100 m — risk of altitude sickness, a night out is mandatory. Fords and snow bridges are unreliable. The alternative North — South road with the Kok-Art tunnel is open only temporarily in 2026 (06:00–20:00, until November) and closes in winter because of avalanches. The petroglyphs are a protected monument: do not touch, trace or write on the stones. There is no signal on the plateau.
food: In Kazarman — home cooking at guesthouses; at the summer pastures on the way — kumis and ayran from shepherds (typical for a jailoo, not confirmed by a specific source).
reviews: Google Maps: a “Saimaluu Tash” marker was found, the rating was not recorded in the cross-check (07.10.2026). Travellers (takali.org 2025, CNN) call the place an impressive “museum under the sky”; cons — a hard climb, late snow, modern vandalism on the stones.
p.sum: Saimaluu-Tash is a 2–3 day expedition in the window of mid-July to mid-August. The trail starts at the Kok-Art River, off the Jalal-Abad — Kazarman road (the new North — South road through the Kok-Art tunnel): from the south you can drive straight from Jalal-Abad, from the north via Kazarman (≈38 km, of which ~28 km is dirt road). Then 7.5 km and +1100 m on foot (4–6 h) or ~5 h on horseback via Besh-Beren, a night in a tent below the petroglyphs (fee 300–400 som + camping 300 som). CBT Kazarman (+996 777 688 803) arranges the jeep, horses and guide.

p.iti.0.title: 2 days from Kazarman
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: 06:00 jeep to the gate (1–1.5 h), a 4–6 h climb, camp by the stones, evening light. Day 2: morning at the petroglyphs, a ~2 h descent, jeep to Kazarman.
p.iti.1.title: 3–4 days including travel
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Jalal-Abad — Kazarman (157 km, via Kok-Art). Days 2–3: Saimaluu-Tash with a night out. Day 4: Kazarman — Naryn or Song-Kol (North — South road).
p.iti.2.title: A combination
p.iti.2.plan: Song-Kol — Ak-Talaa — Kazarman — Saimaluu-Tash — Jalal-Abad — Arslanbob.
p.season: Mid-July — mid-August (CBT Kazarman); in 2023–2024 the snow melted late — better from 20 July. September — first snow. Outside the window — snow, the climb is impossible. By day — hot sun, at night cold.
p.budget.economy: ~6000–9000 som/person: shared taxi Jalal-Abad — Kazarman 600×2 som, a guesthouse ~$15–20, park fee 300–400 + camping 300 som, a share of a jeep/hitchhiking, your own food.
p.budget.comfort: ~$250–400/person for 3–4 days: a driver from Jalal-Abad, a CBT guide 4000–9000 som/day, horses, a guesthouse with meals up to $45.
p.permits: No border permit is needed. Nature park fee 300–400 som + camping 300 som — paid to the ranger at the parking lot (2025). Kok-Art tunnel: cars 100 som (Kyrgyz plates) / 200 som (foreign), cashless only, since 09.07.2026.
p.access: Only for the physically fit: a climb of 1100–1300 m, fords, a night at 3000+ m. For children — teenage age and on horseback. Not accessible for wheelchair users or older people.
